title: Vendor eligibility and rich tile copy playbook
content:
Purpose
--------
Quick working playbook for partner eligibility checks + the ‘rich tile’ metadata/copy we need to ship a marketplace listing that converts and passes technical & legal review. This is intentionally lean — copy variants + technical gates + acceptance tests in one place so PM + Partner Success + Security can iterate without bouncing between docs.

Scope / audience
----------------
- Audience: PMs owning cloud marketplace listings, Partner Success, legal reviewer, partner contact.
- Outcome: A go/no-go checklist and a small bank of copy/art assets that can be dropped into vendor console submission flows.

Key constraints (headlines)
--------------------------
- Tile + short description must be vendor-safe and pass legal review (no unverified claims).
- Graphics: single hero tile + small logo. Acceptable formats: PNG or SVG (logo). Max hero size 1200x675 px, 72dpi.
- Copy lengths (hard limits): short title 40 chars, subtitle 100 chars, long description 1200 chars, 5 feature bullets x 140 chars each.
- Security gates: SSO (SAML/OIDC) supported OR clear justification for SaaS-only model; KMS integration required for private/offers where customer-managed keys are requested.

Eligibility quick-check (first pass)
-----------------------------------
[ ] Legal entity name, tax ID, and address verified
[ ] Partner has public privacy policy + DPA draft available
[ ] Minimum support SLA defined (P1/P2 response windows)
[ ] Pricing model clarified (metered per-token / subscription / reserved capacity)
[ ] No embargoed tech or export issues declared

Technical readiness checklist (must list owners)
------------------------------------------------
- Artifacts needed from partner:
  * High-res logo (SVG) — owner: partner
  * Hero screenshot (1200x675 PNG) — owner: partner/Product
  * API endpoint + test credentials for integration smoke test — owner: partner/engineering
- Infra gates:
  * SAML/OIDC proof-of-concept for sign-on (or tenant isolation spec) — owner: eng-identity
  * KMS proof or documented plan for CMEK if private offers require it — owner: security
  * Billing SKU mapping doc (see sample below) — owner: finance ops

Acceptance criteria (detailed)
-----------------------------
1) Listing copy passes legal review (no performance claims like "100x cheaper" w/o benchmark link).
2) Security review signoff for data handling in the model inference flow (logs, prompt retention).
3) Tech smoke test: sample request to partner endpoint returns schema v1.2 and adheres to rate limit guidance.
4) UX preview: tile displays properly across desktop and mobile mockups (QA checklist attached).

Sample tile metadata and copy variants (drop-in ready)
-----------------------------------------------------
Meta fields: {Title, Subtitle, Long description, 5 bullets, CTA, Tags, Category, Pricing blurb}

A. Enterprise tone (short form)
Title (<=40 chars): Redwood Inference — Secure LLM Serving
Subtitle (<=100 chars): Dedicated inference for regulated workloads with predictable throughput and encryption at rest
Long (<=1200 chars): Redwood’s Dedicated model-serving integrates with enterprise identity and key management to provide predictable, auditable inference for production apps. Ship LLM features with VPC isolation, configurable autoscaling, and per-route observability. Ideal for teams that need SLA-backed latency targets, private model control, and pay-for-reserved capacity.
Bullets (5 x <=140 chars):
- Dedicated GPU pools with per-tenant isolation and burst capacity
- Integrates with customer KMS and SSO providers (SAML/OIDC) for compliance
- Token-level cost analytics and per-route tracing for debugging regressions
- Automated model rollouts: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies
- Suggestions for quantization and batching to reduce unit costs without quality loss
CTA: Try the dedicated trial / Request demo
Tags: inference, dedicated, private-deployments, compliance

B. Startup / developer tone (short form)
Title: Fast LLM inference for devs
Subtitle: Simple API, predictable pricing, free trial credits to get started
Long: Use Redwood’s hosted API for low-latency text generation, streaming responses, and function-calling. Start with public models and scale to dedicated capacity as usage grows. Built-in caching and batching save cost while SDKs speed time-to-product.
Bullets:
- Simple REST + SDKs for text, chat, embeddings
- Streaming responses and function/tool calling
- Free credits, quickstart templates, and sample apps
- Model catalog with curated profiles and cost estimates
- Auto-fallback to compatible variants when capacity is limited
CTA: Sign up and get free credits
Tags: hosted-api, developer, quickstart

Legal & privacy copy (short snippets)
------------------------------------
- Data handling blurb for listing: "Customer data submitted for inference is isolated per account and retained only as described in our Privacy Policy; customers can opt into shorter retention windows or enable CMEK for private deployments."
- DPA note: "DPA available upon request; we support subprocessors list and SOC2 reports"

Billing SKU mapping (example)
---------------------------
- SKU: RDW-DED-1 (Dedicated small) — monthly commit — unit: vGPU-hour
- SKU: RDW-HOST-GEN (Hosted text gen) — unit: token-thousand
- SKU: RDW-EMB-STD — unit: 1k embeddings
Notes: finance needs partner pricing tables and a mapping file (CSV) with effective dates + promo codes.

UX/QA test matrix (quick)
------------------------
- Tile render checks: desktop card, mobile card, hover state, dark-mode preview
- Accessibility: logo alt text present, color contrast > 4.5:1 for CTAs
- Copy fallbacks: ensure long description truncated to ~300 chars in narrow cards
- Link checks: support URL, privacy URL, DPA link all resolve and use https

Preflight timeline (example)
-------------------------
- Day 0: Partner sign-off on copy + logo assets (owner: partner)
- Day 1-3: Security & legal 1st pass (owner: security/legal)
- Day 4-7: Engineering smoke tests + billing mapping (owner: eng/finance)
- Day 8: Final approval meeting + schedule publish (owner: go-to-market)

Open questions / unresolved
--------------------------
- Do we require partners to support OE normalization of model outputs (structured JSON) for listing? (pros: consistent UX, cons: extra dev burden) — need decision from product.
- Private offers flow: who owns CMEK validation with partner infra team? (security to define SLA)

Quick TODOs (work items)
------------------------
- [ ] Pull partner's SOC2 summary and upload to secure drive (owner: Partner Success)
- [ ] Create mobile mock screenshot from hero image (owner: designer)
- [ ] Draft final legal blurb and DPA link (owner: legal)

Notes to self
------------
- If partner claims improved latency/cost, ask for benchmark artifact + test harness. Prefer linked GH action or k6 script we can run in CI.
- Keep tile copy conservative — marketplace reviewers are strict about comparative claims.

Appendix: sample Slack snippets to confirm with partner
------------------------------------------------------
"Quick check: can you confirm the hero image in 1200x675 PNG and an SVG logo? Also, do you have a DPA draft and SOC2 summary we can attach to the listing? Thanks — Sofia (PM)"

End of doc.
